messages:
sara.support: Received an escalation from a customer (internal ticket #SR-9921). They hit a parser error when using JSON/structured output — their downstream JSON parser throws 'Unexpected token' on our response. Posting repro and sample response they pasted.

matt.runtime: Can you drop the request-id and a minimal curl so we can repro? Also which model + structured flags were they using?

sara.support: Minimal repro (customer says this fails consistently):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-structured","input":"List two items with keys 'name' and 'note':\n1) Foo\n2) Bar","structured_output":true,"max_tokens":200}'
```
They get HTTP/200 with a body that is supposed to be JSON. Their parser error: "Invalid JSON at position 487". They pasted the body (redacted):
```
{"items":[{"name":"Foo","note":"Line with a backslash: \\\\ and quote: \"here\""},{"name":"Bar","note":"Emoji: \\ud83d\\ude00\nNewline here"}],"meta":{"model":"redwood-7b-structured"}}
```
Note: I highlighted double-escaped backslashes and a unicode escape that may be split across tokens per their claim.

julio.ml: Thanks. Looks like the model's string tokens include literal backslashes that are being encoded twice on the service side in streaming/structured mode. In some cases the streaming output chunks split inside a Unicode escape (e.g. "\\u" followed by continuation) and our stream-assembler doesn't reassemble before doing JSON validation.

matt.runtime: Repro steps for us: 1) run the same curl with stream=true to mimic their client 2) capture the raw wire frames from the runtime. We should look for chunk boundaries that cut inside an escape sequence.

sara.support: Customer said they were using streaming=true and a small client buffer. They also reported it only happens when the content contains backslashes or quotes (Windows paths, user-entered text).

infra-bot: NEW LOGS AVAILABLE for request-id req_8b2f4c7a (174.56.3.12). Use /logs req_8b2f4c7a to fetch.

matt.runtime: I grabbed the raw stream for req_8b2f4c7a. Snippet of concatenated chunks (raw UTF-8 bytes -> string):
```
{"items":[{"name":"Foo","note":"Line with a backslash: \\\"\n","...}
```
You can see a chunk ended mid-escape and the next chunk started with a quote which produced a `\\\"` sequence when naively concatenated. Our streaming assembler was applying JSON-escaping normalization per-chunk which double-escaped the backslash.

julio.ml: Quick root cause hypothesis: when structured_output is enabled + streaming, we attempt to escape each chunk independently to avoid partial malformed JSON being emitted to clients. That logic inadvertently escapes already-escaped sequences at chunk boundaries. Two potential fixes: A) on the assembler layer, only apply escaping once after full-message reassembly for non-real-time clients; B) implement smarter chunk-merge that detects incomplete escape sequences (regex: /\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{0,3}$/ or trailing backslash) and buffers until completed.

matt.runtime: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: ask customers to set "stream": false or increase client buffer to wait for full message before parsing. Also we can add a gateway-side post-join de-duplication pass to unescape double-escaped backslashes in common patterns.

sara.support: Customer tried setting stream=false and confirmed the output parsed fine. They said latency increase was acceptable for now.

matt.runtime: I'll open an internal issue to implement the correct chunk reassembly logic (avoid per-chunk escaping). Assigning to eng-runtime. Tagging eng-ml to validate no model-side change required.

julio.ml: Will validate model behavior against structured tokens; I don't expect model change needed. Also adding a regression test: streaming structured_output + examples with quotes/backslashes/unicode surrogates to CI.

sara.support: Follow-up to customer: provided workaround (stream=false) and ETA for a fix: next-week patch on runtime assembler. Customer accepted. Closing for now but keeping ticket open until patch ships. :white_check_mark:

matt.runtime: Filed ticket RT-3491 describing: "streaming assembler double-escapes chunk boundary sequences -> causes invalid JSON for strict parsers". Priority P2, target patch in upcoming hotfix.

sara.support: Thanks all. I'll post a short KB article and recommended workaround in the docs: note about streaming structured_output and escape-sensitive payloads.
